title: Buffer and Hootsuite alternative for crypto projects
author: Cryptool
excerpt_html: Schedulers solve the posting problem, not the writing problem. An empty queue on Friday is the same silence as no tool at all.
content_html:
Buffer and Hootsuite are scheduling tools, and they are good ones. You write the posts, put them in a queue, and the tool publishes them on time to every channel. The failure mode is well known to anyone who has run a project's social presence: the queue empties. Publishing was never the hard part, writing consistently was. GTM is a go-to-market app that does the writing as well as the publishing, and it comes with your Cryptool account.

What Buffer and Hootsuite do well

Scheduling, reliably, across a lot of networks, with a shared calendar, approval flows for teams and per-channel analytics. Hootsuite adds social listening and a unified inbox at the enterprise end. If you have someone writing the content and you need it queued, sequenced and reported on, both do that job properly and neither is the problem.

The problem they do not solve

A scheduler assumes a supply of posts. For a small crypto team there is no such supply, because the person who would write them is shipping code or talking to investors. Content stops the moment the team gets busy, which is exactly when visibility matters most, and the scheduler sits there empty. Adding a queue to an empty pipeline does not fill it.

The second gap is scope. Social is one surface. Search is another, and for most projects the people who matter are searching rather than scrolling. A scheduler has nothing to say about whether you rank.

What GTM does

It writes as well as publishes. GTM produces on-brand posts and publishes them across your connected channels, so the input is your brand and positioning rather than a finished draft. That is the difference between a queue and an always-on function.

It covers search, not just social. Search engine optimisation and search engine advertising run alongside the content, so the work that makes a project findable is part of the same system rather than a separate tool nobody opens.

It watches for mentions. Brand mention tracking tells you where and when your project is being discussed, which is the part teams most often discover too late.

It supports the commercial motions. Outreach, sales and partnership or M&A work sit alongside the content, so visibility connects to something rather than existing for its own sake.

It runs continuously. The point is that it does not depend on someone remembering. The work happens in the background whether or not this week was busy.

Choosing between them

If you already have a content writer and you need their output scheduled, approved and measured across many networks, use Buffer or Hootsuite. They are mature at that and GTM is not trying to replace a social media manager's workflow. If your actual problem is that nothing gets written, and the queue is empty because there is nobody to fill it, a scheduler is the wrong shape of tool and GTM is closer to what you need.

Common questions

Does GTM replace a social media manager?

It covers the always-on publishing, SEO and mention tracking that otherwise does not happen at all in a small team. A skilled marketer doing strategy, judgement and relationships is doing something else, and the sensible framing is that GTM handles the continuous work so a person can do the parts that need a person.

Which channels can it publish to?

Your connected social channels. You set up the brand and connect the accounts you want it to post to.

Do I approve posts before they go out?

You set up the brand and connect the channels, and the content is produced on-brand from that setup. How much oversight you want is a matter of how you configure it.

Is GTM free?

It comes with your Cryptool account, like the other apps in the account.

Where do I start?

Open GTM with your Cryptool account, set up your brand, and connect your channels.
